program: Youth suicide-risk therapy funding and insurance navigation
priceScope: Conditional full annual recipient cost against an explicitly judged finite therapy-access channel; not whole-portfolio expected value or a marginal donation offer.

what: Second Wind Fund pays for therapy for eligible Colorado youth at risk of suicide and helps insured families navigate care.
The conditional initial reference combines finite symptom-health benefits with signed caregiver household resources, not deaths prevented or future child salaries.
Full FY2025 expenses are $1.94M; the annual recipient cohort and Denver share remain explicit hypotheses.
strengths: The legal recipient and current direct donation route are clear.
Funded therapy and insurance navigation address different practical barriers to treatment.
Null, adverse, payer-cost and cohort sensitivities expose the assumptions behind the reference.
reservations: The reported 10,000 youth served since 2002 is cumulative, not an annual completed cohort.
Insurance, Medicaid, I Matter and other providers can reduce additionality.
Local utility, sustained outcomes, caregiver net earnings and marginal donation capacity are unmeasured.

sections.what: Second Wind Fund Inc, EIN 73-1701536, funds eligible youth therapy and navigates insurance access. Current family information offers 12 funded sessions; the FY2025 return describes 12–20 sessions. These are dated service descriptions, not measured completed treatment or causal recovery.
sections.monitoring: Request annual unique youth, completed sessions, Denver county residence, repeated/sibling households, sustained symptom outcomes and referral alternatives. The cumulative 10,000 youth and 70,000 sessions since 2002 cannot supply an annual denominator.
sections.qualitative: Fast referral targets and private therapy access are promising mechanisms, but are not proof of incremental QALYs. I Matter offers another public free-session route. The model uses N500 annual youth and Denver share .6 as judgments, not observations; clinical response .4, utility .05 and half-year persistence are hypotheses.
sections.cost: Full FYending June2025 expenses are $1,915,520 plus $24,200 netted direct event costs. The conditional center yields 1.346 health QALYs and 0.09782 signed income-equivalent years, approximately $13.43M per better life. One adult caregiver household proxy per youth is adjusted in deduplication sensitivities. A $1,000 net disposable work/resource gain for 20% of attributed households is already after taxes, benefit withdrawal, commuting and work costs; it is not measured, and is halved for positive overlap. Full $30 access/time cost and health burden apply to every exposed household even with no benefit. Delay .1 is the assumed engagement onset for health and access/resource costs, not immediate costs capitalized into later gains.
sections.funding: FY2023–2025 full annual costs are $1.155M, $1.447M and $1.940M. Government grants and insurance routes form part of the counterfactual. Fundraising claims of $100 per session or $1,250 to save a life do not establish marginal impact; annual program cost $1.491M is only a recognized-cost sensitivity excluding other costs and volunteer resources.

model.costScope: Full statewide FY2025 recognized annual cost; partial finite therapy and caregiver channel, unmeasured navigation/prevention effects are unknown rather than zero. Not allocated Denver spend or a next-gift forecast.
model.geographicAttribution: Pinned ten-county Denver CBSA19740; .6 beneficiary share is judgment because no county-resident distribution was found. Office location is not beneficiary geography.
model.formula: Exposed=N×unique; incremental union=exposed×b; health=(union×response×q×discounted finite duration − exposed×harm×onset discount)×Denver share. Income=0.5×joint household log net resources with positive-only overlap and full access costs, plus distinct payer losses localized once. Better-life price=10×cost/(health+signed income equivalent).
model.counterfactual: Medicaid, private insurance, I Matter free youth therapy, other providers and household support without recipient-funded access.
model.attribution: N500, .5 additionality and .4 clinical response are explicit initial hypotheses; cumulative service reach and referral targets do not identify them.
model.uncertainty: Clinical utility/duration, annual unique youth, sibling overlap, caregiver net resources, volunteer economic costs, alternative care and gift expansion remain unmeasured.
model.nativeOutcomes: Current cumulative reach 10,000 youth since2002 and 12-session funding cap; original FY2025 return 12–20 sessions. No verified annual completed cohort.
